name: IN-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district (R+16) with an incumbent running for reelection
Stutzman holds a large fundraising advantage ($840K raised vs. $136K) plus outside support
No public general-election polling, leaving the forecast reliant on fundamentals
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at only about 5-6%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Republican incumbent Marlin Stutzman: a deep-red district, incumbency, and a roughly six-to-one fundraising edge over Democrat Kelly Thompson, who has just $6,000 on hand. With no polls available and markets showing only a small Democratic chance, the race stays firmly in Republican territory.
model.watch: Any emergence of polling showing Thompson competitive, or a major scandal or late outside spending surge against Stutzman, would be the first sign this is closer than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northeast Indiana's 3rd District is a solidly Republican seat, and incumbent Marlin Stutzman is running for reelection with the advantages that come with it. He has raised about $840,000 to Democrat Kelly Thompson's $136,000, holds a large cash-on-hand lead, and benefits from outside spending on his side. Thompson, a first-time candidate, has minimal cash remaining and no reported outside support.

No public general-election polls are available for this race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Thompson only a small chance of winning. The district's strong Republican lean and the incumbent's resource advantage make an upset unlikely, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
